selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main message of this passage about the earth?
questions.answer: The earth and everything on it point to Allah’s necessary existence and oneness.

questions.question: What is the earth doing in the passage in a figurative sense?
questions.answer: It is giving witness to the truth about Allah.

questions.question: How does the earth support this truth?
questions.answer: Through the many signs found throughout creation.

questions.question: What does “disposition” or ordering teach about the earth?
questions.answer: It shows things are arranged carefully, not left random or chaotic.

questions.question: What does “the giving of life to all animate beings” emphasize about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that life in all its forms depends on Him.

questions.question: How does the passage connect life itself to Allah?
questions.answer: It presents Allah as the giver of life to every living being.

questions.question: How does administration strengthen the passage’s claim?
questions.answer: It shows the world is managed with order and control.

questions.question: Why might the passage call this truth something that can be seen?
questions.answer: Because its evidence appears in the world around us.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly arguing from one miracle or from many signs together?
questions.answer: It argues from many signs together.

questions.question: How would you summarize the passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: The earth, through its order, life, care, and mercy, clearly points to Allah alone as the Creator and Sustainer.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the earth prove?
questions.answer: It proves the necessary existence and oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What is being testified to by that witness?
questions.answer: Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Why is “subjugation” an important part of the evidence?
questions.answer: It shows that creation follows divine command.

questions.question: What can we infer from the mention of nurturing?
questions.answer: Living things need ongoing care, and that care comes from Allah.

questions.question: What does “protection” add that “nurturing” alone does not fully show?
questions.answer: It adds the idea of safeguarding what has been brought into life.

questions.question: Why is the scattering of seeds a meaningful sign?
questions.answer: It shows both continuation of life and careful planning across the earth.

questions.question: What does the phrase about all living beings teach about Allah’s care?
questions.answer: His care reaches every living creature, not just a few.

questions.question: Why does the passage combine mercy with compassion?
questions.answer: To stress both tenderness and broad generosity in Allah’s dealings with creation.

questions.question: What is the effect of ending with compassion and mercy?
questions.answer: It leaves the reader with the understanding that divine rule is full of kindness.

questions.question: What is the best brief summary of the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: The earth’s order, life, protection, and mercy all point to one all-powerful and caring Creator.

questions.question: What statement stands at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: That only Allah is worthy of worship and that His existence is certain.

questions.question: What special quality of Allah is emphasized right after that?
questions.answer: His existence is necessary and not dependent on anything else.

questions.question: In this passage, what serves as the witness for Allah’s existence?
questions.answer: The earth with everything in and on it serves as the witness.

questions.question: What religious truth is declared at the beginning of the statement in this passage?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah.
